title: Lab X-ray CT of fatigue damage in UD non-crimp glass fibre/polyester composite (wind turbine blade material)
material: Uni-directional E-glass non-crimp fabric (NCF) / polyester composite

composition.fibre: glass fibre, uni-directional non-crimp fabric with off-axis backing bundles

chemistry.notes: Fibre volume fraction not verified from accessible sources.

processing.route: Liquid moulding of NCF (details in paper; unverified)

acquisition.notes: Interrupted (ex-situ) scans at two damage levels; medium (MR) and high (HR) resolution tiff stacks; voxel size not verified from accessible text.

defects.statistics: Damage appeared as local UD fibre-fracture regions close to the supporting backing layer, as 3D clusters and chains of fibre fractures (group summary).

fatigue.loading: Tension-tension fatigue, interrupted for CT (parameters in paper)
fatigue.results: Damage progression at two interruption levels (see paper)
fatigue.crack_initiation: Fibre-fracture regions grow from cross-over regions of the backing bundles; backing layer controls location of damage initiation

references.citation: Jespersen KM, Zangenberg J, Lowe T, Withers PJ, Mikkelsen LP. Fatigue damage assessment of uni-directional non-crimp fabric reinforced polyester composite using X-ray computed tomography. Compos Sci Technol 136 (2016) 94-103

notes: DTU Wind Energy / Manchester. Files: MR3 Scan1-3 and HR2-4 tiff stacks plus figure videos.

title: Ex-situ time-lapse X-ray CT of fibre-fracture evolution in NCF glass fibre/polyester under tension-tension fatigue
material: Glass fibre non-crimp fabric reinforced polyester, layup [b/biaxial,b/0,b/0]s

composition.fibre: glass fibre NCF; UD bundles stitched to backing layer of 45/90/-45 bundles

processing.parameters: 410 mm long butterfly-shaped specimen optimised for UD composites, 15 mm wide gauge section

acquisition.volume_dimensions: 1000x1000 pixel projections (2000x2000 detector, binning 2); plus large-field-of-view scan
acquisition.notes: 4x optical magnification, source-sample 28 mm, detector-sample 35 mm, 70 kV; specimen remounted in custom holder and re-registered at each interruption.

defects.statistics: Number of fibre fractures increases with cycles; crack-face separation of broken fibres widens with cycles.

fatigue.loading: Tension-tension, load control, R=0.1, 5 Hz, initial max strain 1%
fatigue.results: Interrupted after 47,300, 57,300, 67,300 and 77,300 cycles for CT of the same region where UD fibre fractures first became visible
fatigue.crack_initiation: UD fibre fractures initiate from matrix cracks in the thin off-axis backing bundles at triple cross-over regions, then spread mainly through the thickness of UD bundles; path depends on local backing bundle arrangement

references.citation: Jespersen KM, Mikkelsen LP. Ex-situ X-ray computed tomography data for a non-crimp fabric based glass fibre composite under fatigue loading. Data in Brief (2017)
Jespersen KM, Mikkelsen LP. Three dimensional fatigue damage evolution in non-crimp glass fibre fabric based composites used for wind turbine blades. Compos Sci Technol 153 (2017) 261-272

notes: A related CT-to-FEM dataset (Avizo/Geomagic/Abaqus workflow) for NCF composite is at 10.5281/zenodo.1244332 (Jespersen et al., ECCM18 2018).

title: NCF glass/polyester fatigue: ex-situ CT of two regions, tension-clamp CT (loaded/unloaded) and in-situ white-light imaging
material: Uni-directional non-crimp glass fabric reinforced polyester

composition.fibre: glass fibre UD NCF with backing bundles

acquisition.notes: High-resolution ex-situ and tension-clamp scans at 2.25 um pixel (5201 projections for tension clamp, ~2 GB each); large-field-of-view scans of all 12 specimens at 19.5 um pixel (1601 projections). Tension-clamp scans taken with and without load applied to open cracks.

fatigue.loading: Tension-tension, R=0.1, 5 Hz; 12 tests at strain levels stated as 0.025% to 0.8% max strain (as written in Data in Brief; verify)
fatigue.results: Ex-situ CT region I at 0, 100k, 150k, 200k, 500k cycles; region II at 150k, 200k, 500k cycles; tension-clamp CT on specimens at 100k and 1M cycles
fatigue.crack_initiation: Fatigue damage initiation and progression studied from backing bundle cracks to UD fibre fractures (Compos Part A 2018)

data_availability.format: TIFF reconstructed volumes, PNG settings, photo zips, MP4/AVI

references.citation: Jespersen KM, Glud JA, Zangenberg J, Hosoi A, Kawada H, Mikkelsen LP. Ex-situ X-ray computed tomography, tension clamp and in-situ transilluminated white light imaging data of non-crimp fabric based fibre composite under fatigue loading. Data in Brief (2018)
Jespersen KM et al. Uncovering the fatigue damage initiation and progression in uni-directional non-crimp fabric reinforced polyester composite. Compos Part A (2018)

title: Correlative time-lapse XCT + DIC of fatigue damage in quasi-UD non-crimp glass/epoxy composite
material: Non-crimp E-glass fabric / epoxy, layup [[0/90]/[90/0]s] with outer cross-woven layers

composition.fibre: E-glass UD bundles stitched to 90 deg backing bundles
composition.layup: [[0/90]/[90/0]s], backing bundles adjacent, sandwiched between 100 um cross-woven fabric layers

processing.route: Composite laminate (NCF); specimens cut by abrasive waterjet (80 mesh garnet)

acquisition.facility: Henry Moseley X-ray Imaging Facility, Manchester: Zeiss Xradia Versa 520 (ROI) and Thermo Fisher Heliscan Mk1 (full field)
acquisition.notes: ROI scans at 0.7 um pixel (4x objective, 70 kV, 20 s/projection) after 0, 70k, 80k, 120k cycles, registered across time steps; one full-field scan at 5.8 um voxel (80 kV) at 0 cycles. DIC strain maps acquired during fatigue.

defects.statistics: Localised cluster of fibre breaks and matrix cracks near backing bundles

fatigue.loading: Tension-tension, load control, 1% max strain, 4 Hz, R=0.1
fatigue.results: Major stiffness drops correlated with number/location of fibre breaks (XCT) and surface strain localisation (DIC)
fatigue.crack_initiation: Fibre-break clusters and matrix cracks near backing bundles; DIC shows backing bundles cause regions of higher strain

data_availability.format: 2D TIFF stacks (zip); DIC .vc7 raw + metadata; MP4

references.citation: Prajapati A, Morse S, Chirazi A, Burnett T, Withers PJ. Complementary time-lapse datasets of x-ray computed tomography and real-time strain mapping for an ex-situ study of non-crimp glass fibre composites under fatigue loading. Data in Brief (2021)

title: In situ synchrotron CT of fatigue micromechanisms and fibre failure in double-edge-notched cross-ply carbon/epoxy
material: Particle-toughened aerospace carbon/epoxy (T700/M21 reported for the related 2017 fast-CT study; untoughened and intrinsically toughened systems also compared)

composition.fibre: carbon fibre (T700 per related 2017 paper; unverified for each fatigue paper)
composition.matrix: epoxy: particle-toughened (M21), untoughened, and intrinsically toughened systems

processing.parameters: Double-edge-notched coupons; in 2017 study: 1 mm central cross-section between notches, 66 mm long, 4 mm wide

acquisition.facility: Synchrotron (beamline not verified from accessible sources; Southampton mu-VIS group)
acquisition.notes: Sub-micron resolution in situ SRCT; voxel size not verified.

mechanical_properties.other: Related monotonic fast SRCT (2017): fewer than 8% of 0 deg fibres fractured at 99.9% of failure load; clusters formed as singular burst events.

fatigue.loading: Tension-tension fatigue of notched coupons, interrupted for in situ SRCT; peak loads up to >70% UTS (R, frequency not verified)
fatigue.results: Fatigue produced significantly more fibre breaks than quasi-static loading at the same peak load; clusters of adjacent breaks above ~70% UTS peak load
fatigue.crack_initiation: Fibre breaks along 0 deg ply splits associated with bridging fibres and in bulk 0 deg plies; particle de-bonding ahead of crack tips and crack bridging by unfailed ligaments (toughened system); resin-rich regions constrain crack propagation in toughened systems; degradation of bridging ligaments in crack wake is critical

references.citation: Garcea SC, Mavrogordato MN, Scott AE, Sinclair I, Spearing SM. Fatigue micromechanism characterisation in carbon fibre reinforced polymers using synchrotron radiation computed tomography. Compos Sci Technol 99 (2014) 23-30

notes: Core in-situ fatigue CT series from Southampton (Garcea PhD 2015). No public data deposit found.

title: In situ SRCT statistics of local fibre misorientation/packing around fibre breaks in carbon/epoxy
material: Carbon/epoxy cross-ply laminates, (90_2/0_2)s (five fibre/sizing/surface-treatment configurations in 2022 study)

composition.fibre: carbon fibre (different sizing types, surface treatments, diameters)

acquisition.notes: Automated segmentation of individual fibres from loaded coupons; facility and voxel not verified.

defects.statistics: Surroundings of damaged sites statistically differ from non-damaged sites in local misorientation; separation distances of adjacent coupled breaks reported

fatigue.crack_initiation: Monotonic tension; fibre-break initiation linked statistically to local fibre misorientation; weaker fibre-matrix adhesion suggested to increase defect tolerance
